Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
938 AM PDT Tue Oct 13 2026

.SYNOPSIS...13/232 AM.

Minor to moderate coastal flooding is likely continue through at 
least Tuesday. A Santa Ana wind pattern will create much warmer
temperatures this week as well as gusty northeast winds at times,
strongest Thursday and Friday.

&&

.SHORT TERM (TDY-THU)...13/937 AM.

***UPDATE***

Moderate offshore trends (2 mb offshore in south and west
directions) has yielded full sun and kicked off the drying trends
with hints of warming to kick off in earnest into Wednesday.

We have increasing confidence in a strong Santa Ana Wind event
peaking Thursday into Friday. We will likely be issuing Wind 
Headlines for the Santa Ana Wind Cooridor of Los Angeles and
Ventura Counties today. A Fire Weather Watch has been
issued for roughly the same areas Thursday and Friday. While Heat
Advisories will likely be issued for ALL coastal areas for 
Thursday through Saturday.

***From Previous Discussion***

The forecast through this weekend remains largely unchanged. A low
pressure system is moving slowly through the Great Basin today and
Wednesday. That will set the stage for a developing Santa Ana wind
event across portions of southern California this week as high
pressure over the Great Basin forces winds up and over the
mountains and down into the valleys and coastal areas. The rapid
acceleration of the air into increasingly higher pressure at 
lower elevations will force the air to heat up significantly (per
the gas law). Will start to see this process as early as today as
the upper low advances to the southeast, allowing the transport of
air from the north to begin. Latest models show just a very light
north-northeast wind developing over the mountains today and 
tonight, then increasing in speeds each day through Friday, by 
which time winds aloft will be around 40-50 mph. In response, 
temperatures across the coast and valleys will warm by roughly 10 
degrees each day, peaking Friday with highs in the upper 80s to 
mid 90s in most areas. There is at least a 60-80% chance of heat 
advisories across many coastal areas on Friday, but much lower 
chances elsewhere since coastal areas are more susceptible to 
heat issues and also coastal areas will probably be warmer than
the valleys (a common result in strong Santa Anas). Mountains and
deserts will warm as well but by much lower amounts.

The Santa Ana winds will be strongest Friday but Thursday likely 
a close second. Most of winds will be confined to LA and Ventura 
Counties where wind advisories and/or warnings will be needed. 
Could see wind gusts into the 60s and 70s in the most favored 
exposed areas of the San Gabriel Mountains. Isolated areas of the 
Central Coast will get gusty winds as well, especially in and 
around the Santa Lucias.

.LONG TERM (FRI-MON)...13/324 AM.

One more day of gusty Santa Ana winds are possible (30-40 percent
chance of reaching advisory levels) into Saturday, taking on a
more easterly orientation.

Temperatures are expected to remain well above normal through 
Sunday, but slowly cooling into next week. And looking out a 
little further there is fairly high agreement in the models that 
another cold upper low will move into the area the middle of next 
week, for another big swing into temperatures and weather
conditions. It looks like mainly a dry system at this point, but
there is some potential is tracks just enough offshore to support
some shower activity.

&&

.AVIATION...13/0006Z.

At 00Z at KLAX, A moist layer was present up to 8000 feet.

Overall, moderate confidence in TAFs. There is a threat of
isolated sprinkles or very light showers across LA county until
sundown. There will be 20-40% chance of MVFR CIGs through early
evening across KLAX, KSMO, KLGB, KBUR, AND KVNY.

KLAX...Moderate confidence in TAF. There is a threat of
isolated sprinkles or very light showers at KLAX until sundown. 
There is a 30% chance of MVFR CIGs through early evening. A slight
north to northeast winds component will most likely develop on 
Tuesday morning, but expected to remain 6 knots or less. 

KBUR...Moderate confidence in TAF. There is a threat of
isolated sprinkles or very light showers at KBUR until sundown. 
There is a 30% chance of MVFR CIGs through early evening. A slight
north to northeast winds component will most likely develop on 
Tuesday morning, but expected to remain 6 knots or less.

&&

.MARINE...13/807 AM.

For the Outer Waters, moderate to high confidence in current
forecast. For the afternoon and evening periods through Wednesday,
there is a 40-60% chance of SCA level winds around Point 
Conception. For Thursday through Saturday, high confidence in 
winds and seas remaining below SCA levels for most of the waters.
The only exception is there is a 20-30% chance of E-NE SCA level
wind gusts across the outer waters south of the Channel Islands
and west to northwest of San Nicholas Island due to Santa Ana
winds during the late night through morning hours Thursday through
Saturday. The highest chances are on Friday.

For the Inner Waters north of Point Sal, moderate to high
confidence in current forecast. Through Wednesday, there is a 30%
chance of SCA level winds in the afternoon and evening hours. 
Otherwise expect conds to remain below SCA levels. 

For the Inner Waters south of Point Conception, moderate 
confidence in current forecast. Through Wednesday, high 
confidence in winds and seas remaining below SCA levels for most 
area, but the only exception is the western half of the Santa 
Barbara Channel where there is a 50% chance of SCA level winds 
Tuesday afternoon and evening. Thursday through Saturday, there 
is a 40-60% chance of SCA level northeast winds from Ventura south
to Santa Monica, strongest during the late night into early
afternoon hours.

Long period swells from the west and the south are affecting the
coastal waters, and can create a confused sea state. This can 
make boating more challenging and dangerous, especially for small 
vessels.

&&

.BEACHES...13/830 AM.

While the peak timing for the most impactful coastal flooding has
passed, there is still a threat of minor to moderate coastal
flooding through today, due to continued high tides and elevated 
surf. The highest tides will occur during the morning and range 
from 7.0 to 7.2 feet this morning, with secondary high tides 
during the evening (around 5 feet). As for elevated surf, a long 
period southerly swell and long period westerly swell will impact 
the coastal waters the next several days.

The Beach Hazards Statement for Santa Barbara South Coast will 
continue into this afternoon for a combination of elevated surf 
and minor tidal overflow during high tides.

A Beach Hazards Statement Tuesday through Thursday morning will 
likely be extended following the Coastal Flood Advisory 
expiration this afternoon for the LA/Ventura County Beaches. This
is due to minor tidal overflow continuing to be possible during 
morning high tides (remaining around 6.5 feet) and the 2 foot 
15-16 second southerly swell continuing to impact the area.

Please continue to monitor the forecast and refer to the Coastal
Hazard Product (CFWLOX) for more information.

&&
